name: Barbell Wrist Curl
grip: Underhand supinated grip with palms facing upward and thumbs under or around the bar, hands shoulder-width apart.
description: Flex the wrists upward against a barbell while forearms rest supported along a bench or thighs with palms facing upward, isolating the deep and superficial wrist flexors.
setup: Kneel beside or sit on the edge of a flat bench holding a loaded barbell with an underhand supinated grip, hands shoulder-width apart.
Rest your forearms flat against the bench pad with wrists and hands extending just beyond the edge.
Keep shoulders relaxed and elbows stationary.
instructions: Lower the barbell by allowing your wrists to extend toward the floor, optionally letting the bar roll gently into your fingers for a deeper stretch.
Curl the bar back into your palms and flex your wrists upward as high as possible, squeezing the inner forearm muscles.
Hold the peak flexion contraction for a brief pause.
Lower the bar slowly under control back to the starting stretch before beginning the next repetition.
cues: Keep forearms glued to the bench pad.
Curl wrists upward toward the ceiling.
Control the lowering phase without bouncing.
commonMistakes: Lifting the elbows or forearms off the bench to assist the lift.
Using heavy loads that force rapid, jerky reps with incomplete wrist range.
Dropping the barbell off the fingertips.

logging.example: Barbell loaded to 20 kg: record 20 kg total barbell mass.
logging.note: Record the total system mass of the barbell plus all loaded plates.

variantNote: Supinated forearm-supported wrist flexion targeting the flexor carpi group. Direct counterpart to the reverse wrist curl.
